name: AI Deep Dive — OKLO — 2026-05-02
rationale: Oklo is a pre-revenue advanced fission (micro-SMR) developer with accelerating cash burn and a binary NRC licensing dependency. At $70.40, the $12.24B market cap prices in a full-scale nuclear renaissance well beyond a 5-year horizon. A first-principles DCF seeded from a $5M pre-commercial baseline yields a probability-weighted fair value of $5.10, implying 93% downside. Even the bull scenario — 20+ Aurora units online by 2030 — produces only $16.34 present value. The stock is pricing on real-options/optionality rather than fundamentals. SELL.

bear.rationale: NRC licensing delayed beyond 2027 (ref: NuScale 2023 failure). Only 1-2 Aurora units deployed by 2030. Capital markets tighten for speculative nuclear, forcing dilutive equity raises. Y5 revenue ~$95M. Thin 5% margin reflects high fixed costs with limited scale. Exit PE 14 = Utilities conservative benchmark. Quality 0.90 = no revenue demonstrated, execution risk dominant.
risks: NRC licensing rejection or multi-year delay (NuScale precedent 2023)
Capital markets close for speculative nuclear, dilutive raises destroy per-share value

base.rationale: NRC licensing approved ~2027. 5-10 Aurora units online by FY2030 (15-50 MW each) under contracted power-purchase agreements. Fuel recycling contributes small but growing revenue. Y5 revenue ~$490M at 12% early-scale margin. Exit PE 18 = Utilities growth ceiling from benchmarks. Ongoing dilution 3%/yr for capex. Base anchored to first-principles commercial ramp from pre-revenue baseline.
risks: Supply chain for exotic fuel (HALEU) disrupts commercial timeline
Power purchase agreement pricing lower than modelled, compressing margins

bull.rationale: Catalyst: NRC fast-track + AI/data-centre power demand (hyperscalers' contracted load) drives 20+ Aurora units deployed by 2030. Fuel recycling fully commercial, adding recurring high-margin revenue stream. Y5 revenue ~$1.2B at 18% margin from modular manufacturing scale. Exit PE 22 = Utilities growth premium (NextEra comparable ~20x). Quality 1.05 = fuel recycling creates early lock-in moat.
risks: AI power demand pivot away from nuclear if efficiency gains reduce load growth
Valuation re-rates downward if bull timeline slips even 12 months

aiThesis.rationale: OKLO is a compelling technological vision priced as though it has already succeeded. The Aurora powerhouse and fuel recycling technology are genuinely differentiated — but a $12.24B market cap for a company with zero revenue, $115M annual cash burn, no NRC approval, and a first commercial reactor still 1-2 years away is pricing in a nuclear renaissance that may or may not materialise within a decade. My first-principles DCF, seeded from a $5M pre-commercial baseline and modelled across three commercial deployment scenarios, yields a weighted fair value of $5.10 — a 93% discount to the current price of $70.40. Even in the bull case (20+ reactors, fuel recycling commercial, $1.2B Y5 revenue), present value is only $16.34. The analyst mean target of $91.36 reflects real-options pricing — a speculative bet on the nuclear renaissance — not a 5-year fundamental model. The stock is not un-investable on a 10+ year thesis, but at this price it prices in extraordinary success that has a low probability of being achieved by 2030. SELL on fundamentals; acknowledge speculative optionality in sizing decisions.

analyticsLog.shareCountMethod: Used metrics.shares_diluted = 173,919,838. shares_outstanding == shares_diluted (no multi-class discrepancy). Piotroski flag no_dilution=false confirms active equity dilution — share count will grow; modelled as +2-4%/yr by scenario.
analyticsLog.marginAnchor: TTM net margin = 0% (pre-revenue; no sales). 4-yr avg = 0% (all zero). Neither standard anchor applicable. Used sector-informed margin path: 5% (bear, early-scale fixed cost drag), 12% (base, modest operating leverage), 18% (bull, modular manufacturing efficiencies). Sector typical range Utilities 10-15% informed the base; Engineering/IPP peers 15-20% informed bull ceiling.
analyticsLog.growthDerivation: Analyst Y1 avg = $235,450 and Y2 avg = $1,142,750 (raw dollars per yfinance — near-zero, not useful for CAGR derivation). Standard ±3pp analyst-anchoring rule cannot apply from a zero base. Used first-principles commercial ramp: seed $5M pre-commercial baseline → bear 80% pa (Y5 ~$95M, 1-2 reactors), base 150% pa (Y5 ~$490M, 5-10 reactors), bull 200% pa (Y5 ~$1.2B, 20+ reactors). Each growth rate reflects a specific commercial deployment count assumption, not an abstract %. Hypergrowth exception documented.
analyticsLog.sectorBenchmarkRow: Utilities — Independent Power Producers. Benchmark row: conservative P/E 12, median P/E 16, growth P/E 20. Bear exitPE=14 (between conservative and median, appropriate for unproven first-generation reactor). Base exitPE=18 (above median, reflecting growth profile). Bull exitPE=22 (above growth ceiling, justified by NextEra comparables at ~20x and fuel recycling moat). All within ±30% of median (16) rule: 14 = -12.5%, 18 = +12.5%, 22 = +37.5% (bull justification: fuel recycling recurring revenue differentiates from pure utility).
dataQualityFlags: PRE-REVENUE: All 5 years of historical revenue = $0. Standard DCF methodology not applicable. Seeded base revenue $5M representing pre-commercial government contracts and design work. All scenario prices are model-derived approximations with very high uncertainty.
ACCELERATING BURN: FCF -$10M, -$16M, -$38.7M, -$115.4M over 4 years — exponentially worsening. Capital raises are near-certain in bear/base; modelled as +3-4%/yr dilution.

ANALYST DATA NEAR-USELESS: Y1 avg $235K and Y2 avg $1.14M revenue estimates reflect placeholder zeroes from analysts who cannot model pre-commercial revenue. Wide dispersion ($0-$6.3M high). Analyst mean price target $91.36 implies real-options/10-yr DCF framework not captured by this 5-yr model.

BINARY NRC RISK: Without NRC Design Approval and Construction Permit, no commercial revenue is possible. This is a regulatory binary event with no guaranteed timeline. NuScale (2023) withdrew its project after $300M+ spent — precedent for failure.
FORWARD PE = -77.66: Company expected to remain deeply loss-making through analyst horizon. EPS estimates: FY2026 -$0.79, FY2027 -$0.94 — losses deepening even as first revenues appear.
analyticsLog.confidenceBreakdown: 0.20/1.0 — Base: 1.0. -0.25 pre-revenue/unproven commercial technology (zero revenue history). -0.20 binary NRC licensing risk (pass/fail with no partial outcome). -0.15 accelerating cash burn with no FCF visibility in 5-yr horizon. -0.10 analyst revenue estimates near-zero/unusable for anchoring. -0.10 5-yr DCF horizon fundamentally mismatched to a 8-12yr commercialisation timeline. Final confidence: 0.20 (very low — speculative/optionality valuation).
